enAudit: G2-311 — the title AND the instruction both promise 'one of them is a question', but item 3 of the render (g2311-fruits.png: 'the fig is next to the box max draws two figs for leo') contains no question at all. The page fails its own promise on 1 of its 3 items; nothing in the generator constrains the second drawn sentence to be interrogative. Either force one interrogative frame per item, or drop the question claim from the title and instruction.

G1-302 item 1 — the tiles are 'feeds / the / avocado. / leo', so the only sentence the child can build is 'Leo feeds the avocado.' A person cannot feed a piece of fruit. This is the recorded 'tom feeds the skateboard' ungated-animacy frame, still live on the fruits theme: the sentence bank picks the FEED frame without checking whether the theme noun is animate.

G2-307 item 1 — 'my camel is very small the camel is in the box' (g2307-animals.png). A camel in a box. Same ungated bank: the IN-THE-BOX frame is applied without checking that the noun plausibly fits a box. G2-311 item 3 uses the same frame on a fig, where it is fine — so the gate needs to be on the noun, not on the frame.

crane / image-vocabulary.js — hits G1-301, G2-287 and every vehicles-theme face that draws it. The vehicles theme renders 'crane' as a crane TRUCK (verified: data-lcs-vocab="crane" on cache/themes-512/vehicles/crane@3x.webp in g1301-vehicles.html), but image-vocabulary.js maps crane to the BIRD in every non-English locale: da Trane, sv Trana, no Trane, de Kranich, nl Kraanvogel, es Grulla, pt Grou, it Gru, fi Kurki. English 'crane' is ambiguous, so the EN page is correct and nobody reviewing English can see it; every other locale labels a crane truck with the word for a bird. In Danish it also happens to have the same letter count (crane / trane = 5), so G1-301's letter boxes fit and nothing errors.

G1-296 and G1-297 (and G1-286 at the wider settings) — the picture rows OVERFLOW the white workspace panel horizontally and icons are clipped at both edges. Measured in the renders: g1296-vehicles.png cards 1, 4 and 5, and g1297-toys.png card 3 (the '20 = _ + _' card). At icon 22 / perRow 5 a 20-item group is 10 per row and does not fit the panel width. A child asked to count the group cannot count the ones that are cut in half.

G2-312 — the title 'How Many Days Later?' describes only ONE of the four questions. The spec's question set is ['stickerDate','after','weekLater','dayOfDate']: find a date, count the days between, a date one week on, and a day of the week. The instruction 'Use the calendar to work out each date' is wrong for two of them as well — Q2 wants a COUNT of days and Q4 wants a WEEKDAY, neither of which is a date.

G1-304, G1-287, G1-286, G1-296, G1-297, G2-311 — the instruction is a STATEMENT ABOUT the page, not an instruction to the child. 'The word bank, the letter boxes and the first letter are all there to help.' / 'Every card on this page doubles a group of pictures.' / 'Bigger groups to double, all the way to twenty.' / 'Two sentences ran together, and one of them is a question.' None of them says what to DO. Every other face in the same families gives an imperative, so this is inconsistency inside the family, not a house style.

G1-300 — the instruction is the bare generic 'Sort each word into the right bin.' Since G1-293 lost its pictures, the ONLY thing now distinguishing these two faces is the word-class pair (nouns vs adjectives here, nouns vs verbs there), and G1-300's instruction does not name it. It remains the one instruction in the batch that could be pasted onto any word-classes page unchanged. Its sibling G1-293 was rewritten to 'Read each word. Is it a naming word or a doing word?' and now names its own pair; G1-300 needs the same treatment.

G1-293 and G1-300 — the page still contradicts its own instruction after the picture removal. Both use the child-friendly terms ('naming word', 'doing word', 'describing word') while the BIN LABELS printed on the page read 'Nouns' / 'Verbs' / 'Adjectives'. A six-year-old is told to sort into two bins that are not the bins in front of them. Either the labels or the wording has to move; this is unaffected by the G1-293 change.

G1-293 vs G2-285 — SCAFFOLD INVERSION introduced by removing the pictures. G1-293 is Grade 1 and now has ten bare word chips; G2-285 is Grade TWO, is otherwise the harder task (three bins, not two), and still gives 'Each noun chip has a picture to help.' The younger children now get less support than the older ones on the same skill. Removing the picture from G1-293 was right on its own terms (it gave the noun away), but the same argument applies to G2-285, and the two faces should be decided together rather than drifting apart.

G1-298 and G1-299 — every card carries a large, prominent empty dotted workspace panel (data-lcs-workspace) and neither the title nor the instruction ever mentions it. 'No pictures to count' tells the child what is absent; nothing tells them what the big white box is for, and it is the single largest element on each card. Still true after these two faces were made themeless.

K-315 — 'Look at the capitals, then write them yourself.' says 'them' (the capital letters) where the task is to copy the WORD, and omits 'twice' although the card provides two writing lines. Its sibling K-311, which has the identical two-blank-line layout, does say 'copy it twice' — so the omission is inconsistent within the family rather than deliberate.

K-313 (and the shipped K-302 / K-303 it inherits from) — the instruction describes only tracing ('Trace the word for just one'), but the left cell of every card also carries a SECOND, empty ruled line for writing the word unaided. The base K-287 instruction does mention that line; the variations dropped it.

K-308 — the orange start dot is drawn on the page and is load-bearing (it is the only marker of where 10 is), but unlike its three siblings K-294 / K-295 / K-296 the instruction never mentions it. Counting backwards is exactly the case where a child most needs to be told where to begin.

G2-313 — 'The bricks climb past twenty, so add in writing as you go.' is not idiomatic English and does not say what to write. It also omits the page's real distinguishing features, which the render shows plainly: the wall is FOUR rows, only the bottom row is given, and the child builds upward.
K-311 — the title 'Copy the Word' is singular for a page of four words; the parallel face K-315 uses the plural 'Copy the Capitals'.

PIPELINE, not English copy, but it silently damages 20 shipped types across 8 locales — build-seo-head.js bandedDescription/assemble strips a trailing '?' or '!' from the instruction and forces a full stop (var m = String(mid).replace(/\s*[.!?]+\s*$/, ''); return lead + '. ' + m + '.' + descTail). Any instruction written as a question therefore ships a meta description in which a question is punctuated as a statement. Counted across the shipped strings files: en 1, de 3, it 3, nl 4, pt 3, sv 1, da 2, no 1, fi 2. Two were Danish (G1-279 'Hvilket tal peger pilen på?' and G2-295 'Hvor meget dyrere er den ene?'); this draft rewrites both as imperatives. NOTE this now also hits G1-293's NEW English instruction, which ends in a question mark and will ship as '...Is it a naming word or a doing word.' in every locale that keeps the interrogative form. No locale panel can see this from its own draft, because it only appears in the assembled description. The fix belongs in assemble(), which should preserve a terminal '?' or '!' instead of overwriting it.

scripts/worksheet-gen/tools/validate-b2var-draft.js — the docblock says the gate checks 'exactly the 64 face ids from tools/gen-b2var-specs.js'; ROWS is 100 and the code does check 100. Stale comment, no functional effect, but it contradicts the brief's own count and would mislead the next reader.

G1-302 / data/b2/sentences.js — the capitalised NAME tile gives the answer away in Danish, and this is structural, not a seed. G1-249 lowercases only token 0 and only when index 0 is not a protected capital, so a name at index 0 survives. Measured: ALL NINE Danish {name} frames (s1, s2, s4, s6, s7, s9, s11, s13, s16) put the name at index 0, and there is no Danish frame with a name only mid-sentence — so whenever a name frame is drawn, the one capitalised tile IS the first word. The generated da page proves it: four lanes, data-lcs-caps="0" on every one (William / Alma / Ida / William). The general engine defence that "a capital marks a NAME, not a sentence start" is sound but does not hold for the da bank as written, so "Find the Beginning" is solved by looking for the capital. The Danish copy has been written not to lean on that cue, but the fix is either to lowercase a sentence-initial name when showCap is false (accepting the child sees "william") or to add da frames with the name mid-sentence.
